summary: Precompute cumulative sums (or counts) so that the sum of any subrange can be retrieved in O(1), turning repeated range-sum queries or subarray-sum-equals-target problems into a single pass.
lesson: If you're going to ask "what's the sum of this subrange" many times over an array that doesn't change, it's wasteful to re-add the same numbers on every query. Prefix sum precomputes a running total once, so the sum of any subrange becomes a single subtraction: sum(i, j) = prefix[j] - prefix[i]. The same idea generalizes to counting: if you're looking for subarrays that sum to a target, you can reframe the condition as "has this exact prefix value occurred before," and answer it with a hashmap in one pass instead of checking every subarray. It trades one O(n) setup pass for O(1) answers afterward.
recognize_when: You need many range-sum queries over an otherwise static array
The problem asks for the number/length of subarrays whose sum equals (or is divisible by) some target
A brute force would recompute the sum of overlapping subarrays repeatedly (O(n^2) or worse)
You can reframe the condition as prefix[j] - prefix[i] == target, hinting at a hashmap of seen prefix sums
2D grid versions ask for sums over rectangular subregions

complexity.notes: Building the prefix array/hashmap is a single O(n) pass; each query or lookup afterward is O(1). Space is O(n) for the prefix array (or O(1) extra if only a running sum and hashmap of counts are kept).

template:
def prefix_sum_subarray_count(nums, target):
    from collections import defaultdict
    prefix_counts = defaultdict(int)
    prefix_counts[0] = 1
    running_sum = 0
    count = 0
    for num in nums:
        running_sum += num
        count += prefix_counts[running_sum - target]
        prefix_counts[running_sum] += 1
    return count
gotchas: Forgetting to seed prefix_counts[0] = 1, which breaks counting subarrays that start at index 0
Off-by-one when converting between prefix-array indices and original array indices (prefix[i] represents sum of first i elements, not including index i)
Using a plain running sum without a hashmap when duplicates of the same partial sum matter, losing the ability to count multiple valid subarrays
